doc.title: Butch Cage and Robert Pete Williams Interview, 1967-05-13

chapter: Cage on work songs, church and social life
title: Baptism and 'Under the Bamboo Tree'
summary: Cage describes being baptised in the Mississippi River, and recalls 'Under the Bamboo Tree'.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: And tell me about baptism. Do people sing at baptisms when they put you in the water?

They talk to you. You know the preacher get up and talk about it. You know the preacher, you're baptized according to your fashion. In the name of the father and son all the way. Then they put you in.
Well I thought they had some songs that sang it when you were there. Oh they do sing.
That's a, I can't sing it all now.
Do you ever remember that song about under the bamboo tree? No sir. If you like a me like I like a you. Oh I know that. That's a. That's the one I'm talking about. Oh yeah sir. I know it.
